title: kith-peer: stored attachment sha256 is never verified against blob content
description: validate_attachments checks sha256 is 64-char lowercase hex (format only). The actual blob bytes are never fetched or hashed to verify the claim. A peer can store an arbitrary sha256 value in the DB. Future code that uses sha256 for integrity checking (e.g. a download endpoint) would get a misleading result. This is a Phase 1 known gap (no blob fetching during delivery), but should be documented and addressed before any integrity-critical feature is built on top.
